title: Motovun with Kids: Family Apartments & Activities 2027
metaDescription: Where to stay in Motovun with children, which activities work for kids, what the walls and truffle hunts cost in euros, and how to handle the hill.
content:
## Where to Stay in Motovun with Kids

Motovun stands about 277 m above the Mirna River valley. Every accommodation choice comes down to one question: how far is the bed from the car?

### Old town apartments vs. apartments below the hill

**Old town apartments** put restaurants, the main square and the walls within a few minutes on foot. Apartments Galerija Motovun is one example. It is a short walk from the main square, restaurants and a coffee bar, and it lets children aged 0–7 stay free. The drawback is the cobblestones. Streets are steep and uneven, and some stones are missing, so strollers struggle.

**Villas and apartments below the hill** give families a garden, a pool or room for ball games, plus parking at the door. Many listings around Motovun describe properties with table tennis, badminton or football on site. Villa Fragola, Loggia Motovun and Casa Pino Pina appear among the most popular family-oriented rentals in the area.

The old town sounds like the obvious base, but with a toddler or a stroller it is usually the wrong one. Luggage, groceries and tired children all have to be carried over cobbles. A rental with its own parking and a garden is easier for most families, and the old town is a short drive away.

### What to check before booking

- **Parking:** Cars are restricted at the top. A large car park sits north of the town, about a 15-minute uphill walk from the old town, and a shuttle bus also runs.
- **Kitchen:** Truffle pasta starters in the old town start around €24, so a kitchen saves money for a family of four.
- **Pool fencing and stairs:** Ask about both if children are under 6.
- **Child pricing:** Policies differ. Galerija Motovun's free stay ends at age 7.
- **Air conditioning:** Needed in July and August.

## Best Things to Do in Motovun with Children

### Walk the city walls

The walls are open from about 10:00 to 19:00 in season and cost about €5 per person. Family tickets are reported to exist, so ask at the tourism office on the main square. Entry is free from November to March. The ticket is often part of a combined Motovun Impressions ticket that can include the church, the loggia and the New Gate tower. The circuit takes 30–45 minutes.

The views over the Mirna Valley are excellent, but some visitors find €5 steep for the part of the wall that is open. Children aged 5–10 usually enjoy it. Under 4, skip the ticket. The town square has views too, and the walls have drops.

### Follow the Veli Jože legend

Local legend says giants built the town, and the giant Veli Jože is the best-known figure. Telling the story on the way up turns a hot climb into a game for younger children. Look for the two rings of walls and the 12th-century citadel at the top.

### Go truffle hunting

Motovun forest is known for black and white truffles. Guided hunts with trained dogs take about one hour in the woods and are the most popular activity for children. Miro Tartufi and Tartufi Istra are two operators in the area. Expect to pay about €40 per person.

One reviewer found this expensive for 20 minutes of talk plus a 30-minute walk. Ask the operator how long the forest walk lasts before booking. The dogs are the real attraction for children, and a hunt is better with kids than a restaurant truffle tasting. White truffle season runs September to November. Black truffles can be found for more of the year.

### Cycle or walk the Parenzana

The Parenzana is a former railway line, now a cycling and walking route. Its gentle gradients make it far easier than the hill streets. Choose short sections and stop in small villages along the way, in line with your children's energy.

### Day trips from Motovun

- **Aquapark Istralandia (near Brtonigla):** about 22 km away, the best option for hot summer days.
- **Pazin Castle:** about 21 km away, with a medieval castle that suits school-age children.
- **Coast:** Poreč and Rovinj are the nearest beach towns. Rovinj is about 45 minutes by car.

## Practical Tips for Families

- **Time needed:** Half a day covers the old town, walls and lunch. Add a full day for truffle hunting or the Parenzana.
- **Best hours:** Arrive before 10:00 or after 17:00. Tour buses fill the lanes at midday.
- **Shoes:** Closed shoes with grip. The cobbles are slippery when wet.
- **Tickets:** Buy wall tickets at the tourism office on the main square.
- **Eating:** Ask restaurants for fuži (Istrian pasta) without truffle for children. Kitchen apartments let you cook simple meals.
- **Summer heat:** The climb is exposed. Take water and plan walls for the early morning.
- **Motovun Film Festival:** The festival is held annually. Book accommodation far in advance for that week.

## When to Visit Motovun with Children

**May–June and September** offer warm weather and fewer crowds. **July–August** is hot and busy, and a pool pays for itself. **October–November** suits families interested in white truffle season. The walls are free from November to March, though some restaurants and shops close out of season.

faq.question: Is Motovun good for kids?
faq.answer: Yes, for children aged 4 and up who enjoy walls, legends and short walks. The steep cobbled streets make strollers difficult. Combine the old town with truffle hunting or the Parenzana trail.

faq.question: How much does it cost to walk the Motovun city walls?
faq.answer: Entry is about €5 per person, and family tickets are reported to exist. The walls are free from November to March. Opening hours in season are about 10:00 to 19:00.

faq.question: Where should families stay in Motovun?
faq.answer: Families with strollers or toddlers do best in an apartment or villa below the hill with parking and a garden. Families with older children can stay in the old town, for example at Apartments Galerija Motovun, where children aged 0–7 stay free.

faq.question: Is truffle hunting suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, the dogs and the forest walk keep most children interested. A guided hunt takes about one hour and costs about €40 per person. Ask the operator about forest walk length and any child discount before booking.

faq.question: How much time do you need in Motovun with kids?
faq.answer: Half a day is enough for the old town, the walls and lunch. A full day lets you add truffle hunting or a section of the Parenzana trail.

faq.question: Are there water parks near Motovun?
faq.answer: Aquapark Istralandia near Brtonigla is about 22 km from Motovun. It is the nearest water park and works well on hot summer days.

quickAnswer: Motovun suits families with children aged 4 and up who like castles, walls and short walks. Stay in an apartment with parking, either just below the hill or in the old town. Main activities are the city walls (about €5), a truffle hunt (about €40 per person) and the Parenzana trail.
